A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UNCERTAINTY-LINE study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are available and sufficiently readable for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original length-bias analyses, uncertainty-estimation experiments on translation, summarization and mathematical reasoning, and polynomial-detrending ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds TokenSAR evaluations and experiments comparing 500 quality labels with full-sample fitting.

M1.justification: The core regression and correction equations (1)-(4) remain unchanged. Appendix D.2 adds a limited fitting adaptation that selects quality labels through length trimming and balanced sampling from K-means bins before fitting the existing quality-length regression.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WMT14/WMT19 language pairs, XSum summarization and GSM8K mathematical reasoning. The reduced-label experiment changes sample selection within retained coverage, without introducing a new task or domain.

E2.justification: v2 adds TokenSAR and its LINE-transformed counterpart to the six existing uncertainty estimators. Their participation is documented in Tables 3 and 10-16, including the polynomial comparisons; the original comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 introduces a 500-label versus full-sample comparison with percentile trimming, length rescaling and balanced sampling. The stated MetricX variant also changes from L/Large to XXL, although v1 already used XXL labels elsewhere, so this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.2 tests sensitivity to the number of quality labels on XSum and GSM8K with Llama and Gemma. The existing polynomial-degree ablation is retained and extended to TokenSAR, whose length dependence is also added to Tables 7-9.

E5.justification: Table 3 already reported means with plus/minus quantities in v1; v2 identifies those quantities as standard errors of the mean. Wald tests remain unchanged, and neither version provides new evidence of increased repeated runs or additional seed-based uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The original six methods' detailed PRR scores are retained, while TokenSAR results and 500-label results are added; the latter differ from full-sample fits by at most 0.01 at reported precision. Summary corrections include Table 1's Llama XComet WMT14 Cs-En Base/LINE values changing from 0.47/0.54 to 0.40/0.48, matching v1's Table 12. Table 2 corrects Gemma's XSum baseline from 0.33 to 0.35, and Table 4 revises MetricX slopes and p-values. These are additions and corrections, not demonstrated performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: The regression formulation, assumptions, correction equations and PRR definition are retained. Appendix B adds an explanatory formula for the TokenSAR baseline, without introducing a new theoretical result, proof or derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that length bias persists after normalization and that post-hoc regression correction improves uncertainty estimation across the evaluated tasks. The supervised extension newly highlighted in the introduction already appeared in v1's Section 4.2.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets the existing polynomial experiments as showing no consistent advantage over linear fitting, qualifies translation length-invariance to the evaluated datasets, and refines the labeling limitation with evidence that 500 generations suffice in the new experiment. The principal applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future implementation release; v2 reports public release and supplies a repository link. Appendix D.2 adds reproducibility details for the reduced-label procedure, including percentile thresholds, rescaling, K-means bins and sampling without replacement. Repository availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: Related work adds Duan et al. on TokenSAR, Santilli et al. on response-length confounding, and Li et al. on uncertainty correction. It more explicitly distinguishes calibration methods from length-bias removal and replaces the Llama 2 reference with the Llama 3 paper.

P1.justification: v2 tightens prose in the introduction, related work, evaluation and discussion, exchanges the order of Conclusion and Limitations, and adds acknowledgments and an equal-contribution note. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Several plots receive revised titles, labels and legends; Figure 3 moves, tables gain TokenSAR entries, Table 17 is added, and Tables 15-16 occupy separate pages. New display defects include duplicating the XSum PPL panel in place of MTE in Figure 1 and mis-typesetting TokenSAR's normalization formula in Appendix B.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens empirical support through TokenSAR comparisons and the reduced-label experiment, clarifies SEM reporting, and corrects summary values that contradicted v1's appendix. It also provides code-access information. These gains outweigh localized new presentation defects in Figure 1 and the TokenSAR formula, but the retained scientific contribution and remaining documentation limitations make the improvement incremental.
